title: Orientation-Dependent Universality of Spin-Transport Fluctuations in Two-Dimensional Altermagnets
authors: Yihan Zhang, Zheng Qin, Donghui Xu, Junjie Zeng, Zhen Ning, Rui Wang
abstract: Universal conductance fluctuations are conventionally organized by symmetry class, but crystalline anisotropy introduces additional structure in spin transport. Here we demonstrate orientation-dependent universal spin-transport fluctuations in disordered two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling. Rotating the altermagnetic orientation changes both longitudinal spin-conductance and transverse spin-Hall conductance fluctuations, while each conserved-spin sector remains in class AI. Altermagnetic orientation controls both the fluctuation amplitudes and the development of disorder-insensitive plateaus. These plateaus become flatter and less sensitive to the altermagnetic strength over the studied parameter ranges as the orientation approaches $45^\circ$, with representative fluctuation amplitudes of approximately $0.60e/(4π)$ for the longitudinal spin conductance and $0.40\,e/(4π)$ for the spin-Hall conductance. The longitudinal fluctuation amplitude correlates strongly with anisotropy of the clean-band Fermi-velocity tensor. Spin-sector covariances explain how the conserved channels combine into total fluctuations. Our results extend anisotropy-sensitive universal-fluctuation physics to conserved-spin altermagnetic transport and establish crystalline orientation as a control parameter within a fixed symmetry class.
summary: This work explores orientation-dependent universal spin-transport fluctuations in disordered 2D altermagnets. By analyzing the Hamiltonian's dependence on the crystal angle $\theta$, the authors show that this orientation controls the magnitude of spin-conductance fluctuations. This establishes crystalline anisotropy as a key tuning knob for spin transport properties within a fixed symmetry framework.
main_problem: The paper investigates how crystalline anisotropy influences universal spin-transport fluctuations in disordered two-dimensional altermagnets.
main_result: The orientation of the crystal lattice acts as a control parameter, modulating both the amplitude of spin-transport fluctuations and the stability of disorder-insensitive plateaus.
method: The study employs a disordered lattice model analyzed using non-equilibrium Green’s functions and the Landauer-Büttiker formalism to calculate spin-conductance fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system is a disordered two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet without spin-orbit coupling, modeled by a spinful tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating anisotropic hopping terms dependent on the crystal orientation angle $\theta$.
key_observables: Longitudinal spin-conductance fluctuations ($	ext{rms}(\sigma_s)$) and transverse spin-Hall conductance fluctuations ($	ext{rms}(\sigma_{sH})$).
important_parameters: Crystalline orientation angle $\theta$, disorder strength $W$, and the altermagnetic coupling strength $t_{	ext{AM}}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the absence of spin-orbit coupling, and the effective symmetry within each spin block is classified as Class AI.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the tight-binding model, spin-resolved band structures, and plots showing the angular dependence of fluctuation amplitudes ($	ext{rms}(\sigma_s)$ and $	ext{rms}(\sigma_{sH})$) relative to the anisotropy tensor.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by introducing the anisotropic Hamiltonian, calculates the spin-transport observables using Green's functions, and then systematically analyzes how the orientation angle $\theta$ controls the magnitude and behavior of these universal fluctuations.
why_interesting: The concept of using crystalline orientation as a tunable control parameter within a fixed symmetry class is highly relevant for designing quantum materials where transport properties can be engineered via structural control.
